chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Ali ibn Rashid who said:

I asked him about the Fitrah (alms of fasting), for whom is it? He said, 'For the Imam.' I said to him, 'So should I inform my companions?' He said, 'Yes, whoever you wish to purify from among them.' And he said, 'There is no harm if the price of that is given and carried as silver coins (dirhams).'
And from him (Muhammad ibn Ya'qub) from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdillah from Abdillah ibn Ja'far from Ayub ibn Nuh who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that some people ask me about the Fitrah, and they ask me to carry its value to you. This man had sent to you last year, and he asked me to ask you, but I forgot that. And this year he has sent to you for every head of his dependents one dirham, for the value of nine Artal of dates, one dirham. What is your opinion, may I be your ransom, in this matter? He wrote (peace be upon him): 'The Fitrah, much questioning has occurred about it, and I dislike everything that leads to fame (publicity). So cut off the mention of it. Collect from whoever pays it, and withhold from whoever does not pay it.'
And from him from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his brother Abdillah ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said:

I sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) dirhams for myself and for others, and I wrote to him informing him that they are from the Fitrah of the dependents. He wrote in his hand: 'I received and accepted.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah (alms of fasting paid at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to receive the Fitrah alms and can it be paid in money?
ai.summary: These narrations from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarify that Fitrah is primarily the right of the Imam, who may delegate its collection or accept monetary equivalents (dirhams) for dates, reflecting the practical flexibility of Shia jurisprudence. The Imam’s advice to avoid publicizing payments underscores the virtue of *khufya* (discretion) to prevent *al-shuhrat* (fame/showing off), a key ethical consideration in Shia acts of worship. This establishes a precedent for both the financial nature of Fitrah and the spiritual importance of modesty in charitable giving.
